name: Wallapop
tagline: Spanish-first classifieds app for buying and selling used stuff locally, with optional shipping and paid visibility boosts.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified. Listing is free, revenue comes from bumps, featured slots, shipping fees and pro accounts.

verdictSummary: The app itself is a photo grid, a chat thread and a geo search. All of that is a normal afternoon for a coding agent. The part you cannot build is the several million people in your metro area who already open Wallapop when they want a used bike, plus the payment escrow, the shipping labels and the ratings history that make strangers willing to meet you in a parking lot. A personal clone is a catalog of your own junk that nobody visits. Sell on the marketplace, and build tooling around it instead of under it.
coreLoopDIY: A local, single-user catalog of the things you are selling: photos, prices, notes, sold status, and auto-drafted listing text you paste into the real marketplaces.
requirements: Optional OpenAI-compatible API key if you want generated listing copy
whatYouLose: Escrow payments and buyer protection, so every remote sale becomes a trust exercise
Integrated shipping labels and pickup points
Chat, reputation scores and the social proof that gets a reply in ten minutes
Native iOS and Android apps with camera flow and push notifications
moatNotes: Liquidity is regional: Wallapop is dominant in Spain and Italy, which is exactly why a clone there is even more hopeless than a clone elsewhere.
whyPeopleStillPay: Almost nobody pays to use Wallapop; they pay to be seen on it. A bump or a featured slot is a bid for attention inside a crowd you did not have to gather, and the fee is trivially worth it if it moves a sofa this week instead of next month. Sellers also pay indirectly through shipping and payment fees because the alternative is arguing with a stranger about whether a bank transfer cleared. The product is the crowd and the referee, and neither ships in a repo.
notes: The UI is an afternoon, the demand is not. The moat is regional marketplace liquidity plus the escrow and ratings layer that makes strangers trust each other.
prompt:
Build a local, single-user "stuff I am selling" manager. This is not a marketplace, it is seller-side tooling for someone who lists on Wallapop, Vinted, Facebook Marketplace and similar.

Stack, no substitutions:
- Next.js 15 with the App Router, TypeScript, Tailwind.
- SQLite via better-sqlite3, file at ./data/app.db, migrations in a single SQL file run on boot.
- Photos stored on local disk under ./data/photos, served through a route handler. No S3, no cloud.
- No auth, no accounts, no telemetry. It runs on localhost.

Data model:
- item: id, title, description, category, condition (new / like-new / good / fair / for-parts), askPrice, floorPrice, currency, status (draft / listed / reserved / sold / archived), acquiredCost, createdAt, soldAt, soldPrice, buyerNote.
- photo: id, itemId, filename, sortOrder.
- listing: id, itemId, platform (free text), url, listedAt, bumpedAt, notes.

Screens:
1. Grid of items with photo thumbnail, price, status pill, and filters by status and category.
2. Item editor: drag-and-drop multiple photos, reorder them, edit all fields, add or remove platform listings with URLs.
3. Listing composer: for the selected item, generate a title under 50 characters, a description, and 5 search keywords, in a chosen language (English, Spanish, Italian). Use an OpenAI-compatible chat completion with OPENAI_API_KEY and OPENAI_BASE_URL from .env. If the key is missing, fall back to a deterministic template built from the item fields. Always show a copy button per field.
4. Dashboard: total items listed, sold count, gross revenue, margin over acquiredCost, median days from listed to sold, and a list of items listed more than 21 days ago with a "consider a price cut" flag.

Extras that are in scope:
- A "stale bump" reminder list based on bumpedAt.
- CSV export of all items and sales.
- A single-file JSON backup and restore.

Explicitly out of scope, do not build: any public buyer-facing storefront, in-app chat, payments, shipping labels, or scraping of any marketplace. Do not attempt to auto-post to any platform; the composer produces text for a human to paste.

Deliver: working app, README with setup, .env.example with OPENAI_API_KEY and OPENAI_BASE_URL, npm run dev starts on port 3000 with the database seeded with three example items.
